liposarcoma.label: Day 1: eribulin

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.timing: The team specifies prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and the actual support prescription; this reference does not authorise self-treatment.

additional_support: This is a low nausea/vomiting-risk regimen. Agree individual anti-sickness and bowel support; National Cancer Control Programme lists no usual separate premedication. White-cell growth-factor support may be chosen for severe neutropenia, but there is no universal routine course.

Bring all medicines and report numbness, weakness, constipation, infection or fainting before treatment. Review medicines that affect heart rhythm. Arrange written contraception instructions and avoid breastfeeding during treatment.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
An improved test result does not authorise restarting after a safety hold; confirm the new prescription.

Metoclopramide: adult maximum 10 mg up to three times daily (30 mg/day) and maximum treatment duration 5 days under current European Medicines Agency/Irish product information; avoid prolonged repeated use without review.
Review heart-rhythm risk and electrolytes before choosing anti-sickness medicines that can affect the QT electrical interval.

local_reference.label: CUH Department of Medical Oncology: Adjuvant medication prescription for chemotherapy Low Risk for nausea and vomiting, Version 2 (05/05/2021)
local_reference.note: The local CUH source is retained as a reference list, not as the national antiemetic standard. Nystatin/chlorhexidine are displayed as local mouth-care adjuncts, not universal antiemetic or mucositis prophylaxis. Verify current local oral-care policy. This historical local proforma needs current pharmacy confirmation. It is an alternative reference, not a second course to add automatically.

items.directions: Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.

sarcoma.label: Day 1: pegylated liposomal doxorubicin

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.timing: The team specifies prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and the actual support prescription; this reference does not authorise self-treatment.

additional_support: National Cancer Control Programme classifies this as low nausea/vomiting risk and lists no usual premedication. Follow individual anti-sickness and mouth-care advice. For 4–7 days after treatment, avoid excessive heat, friction and tight pressure on hands or feet; cooling measures and any skin treatment follow the local plan. Do not start routine vitamin or steroid hand–foot prophylaxis yourself.

Confirm the exact pegylated liposomal product and all previous anthracycline doses. Report heart symptoms, mouth ulcers and painful hands or feet before the visit. Review interacting medicines, pregnancy precautions and any prior infusion reaction.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
An improved test result does not authorise restarting after a safety hold; confirm the new prescription.

Metoclopramide: adult maximum 10 mg up to three times daily (30 mg/day) and maximum treatment duration 5 days under current European Medicines Agency/Irish product information; avoid prolonged repeated use without review.
